en: The *Sūtra of the Youth of the Devaputra Pingala*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daixingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Wisdom,
who was a Special Advancement and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, by Imperial Decree.
If there is a practitioner who upholds this vidyā,
whether they beg for food, subsist exclusively on milk porridge, or eat ordinary food,
they should recite it thirty thousand times before an image.
Thereafter, perform the fire ritual:
take jade and fashion it into one thousand and eight pieces;
recite the mantra once and cast each piece into the fire.
If one performs this three times daily for forty days,
it is said that whatever one seeks shall be fulfilled.
Furthermore, one may take *yūka* (jasmine) and *anusthāna* incense to form pills.
Beginning on the eighth day of the dark fortnight and concluding on the fourteenth day,
recite one thousand and eight times at each of the three daily sessions. At each session,
cast one of the aforementioned pills into the fire.
Whether by day or by night, that youth will invariably manifest his form to become a companion, fulfilling all wishes;
he may be commanded as one pleases, and there shall be nothing he does not accomplish.
Furthermore, there is another method: take guggulu incense and form it into pills.
For seven days, perform one thousand and eight recitations three times each day.
Reciting the mantra once and casting one pellet into the fire each time, one will certainly obtain the position of village headman; there is no goal that will not be accomplished.
When the practitioner wishes to perform this rite:
First, one should recite [the mantra] seven hundred thousand times.
Regarding the method for crafting the image: the image shall be made of white sandalwood.
Six finger-widths in height and in the form of a youth,
his left hand holds fruit while his right hand hangs down in the *varada-mudrā* with the palm facing outward;
place him within the ritual arena (*maṇḍala*).
Prepare various foods, milk porridge, incense, and flowers as offerings.
Take red flowers;
for each flower, recite the mantra once and cast it upon the body of the youth.
If one recites it one hundred thousand times, the youth will certainly manifest his form.
One will then immediately fulfill all wishes;
daily, one will provide superior clothing and food to a thousand people, with nothing lacking.
Furthermore, according to another method, one should take three sessions each day,
preparing one thousand and eight pills of *sugandhaka* (stacte) incense during each session.
After seven full days have passed while [the pills] are in the fire, [the rite is complete].
That youth manifests his form to point out hidden treasures (*nidhi*).
If one can maintain this practice daily, one will obtain great benefit; he will reveal the locations of his treasure caches, and the same applies to the caves and lairs of the asuras.
If one receives instruction [in this practice], one’s wishes will surely be fulfilled and one shall obtain great wealth and treasures. If a person is bound or imprisoned,
by reciting this vidyā-mantra, they shall immediately attain liberation.
Furthermore, there is a method by which one may cause all people to feel joy upon seeing them:
by reciting [the mantra] while calling that person's name one hundred thousand times, they will all rejoice.
Furthermore, there is a method involving taking wood from the *aśoka* tree.
Burn it on a high mountain peak.
Mix it with *guggulu* incense to form one thousand and eight pills and cast them into the fire.
One will immediately attain stability and accomplishment; if one wishes for someone to appear, they shall appear, and one’s lifespan shall reach one thousand years.
The dhāraṇī mantra is:
Oṃ jve jve ni svāhā. Furthermore, another version states: [Oṃ jve jve ni svāhā].
Oṃ jve jve ni svāhā. As for the fundamental mudrā:
join the two hands with palms hollowed together.
When summoning or inviting, move the middle fingers (the wisdom fingers) back and forth.
When performing the dismissal, wave [the ritual implements] outside three times.
The mantra for inviting the Fire Deity and the seal is as follows: Oṃ āgneye agne agne svāhā. The mantra for dismissal is as follows:
Oṃ ākarṣaya gaccha gaccha svāhā. As for the mudrā of this mantra:
bend the right thumb into the palm.
Bend the index finger into a hook-like shape,
using it to press against the back of the thumb at its lower joint;
extend all the other fingers.
When summoning, simply beckon three times with the index finger.
When dispatching, it is the same as waving the hand outward three times.
The mantra for the protection seal is as follows:
Oṃ kuru-dhāna hūṃ jaḥ. As for this mudrā: form a fist with the right hand and extend the thumb to touch five places on the body;
this provides protection against all that has not yet arisen.

This *Bingjie Luo Tian Tongzi Jing* (Sūtra of the Youth Bingjie Luo Tian) was transcribed at Zhongchuan on the twenty-third day of the seventh month in the third year of the Baoyan era. It was proofread and finalized on the twentieth day of the twelfth month in the Jia-wu year of the Cheng’an era (1354). This manuscript was transmitted by collating three versions, based upon the Xuanzheng edition.
